# Pandamonium v1.0.77

This patch train keeps the protected updater fast on installations that carry extension runtimes. It is a follow-up to the v1.0.73 backup-manifest repair: the verified pre-update backup no longer archives data that can be re-derived, so a normal one-click update returns to the ~2 minute window instead of ~20 minutes. No dependency, route, plugin-contract, schema, authentication, or stored-data change. Rollback remains signed v1.0.76 and the updater's retained pre-update snapshot.

## MAD-973 — Updater: skip re-derivable extension data in verified backups

### Problem

Every update takes a verified full-data backup and rehearses migrations twice on a copy of it. That backup walked the entire canonical data directory, including `data/extension-runtimes` (per-package Go toolchains, module caches, and build caches) and `data/extensions/removed` (the uninstall graveyard that is never read back). On CT103 the marketplace and Entertainment work grew those trees until the data directory reached 3.2 GB, and each updater transaction then consumed about 20 minutes of CPU. The owner-visible progress panel parked at 55% ("Rehearsing migrations twice on backup data") for most of that time, so a successful update looked hung. The backup command already carried a `_SKIP_PATTERNS` comment about skipping re-derivable data, but the set was dead code and never applied.

### Implementation

`scripts/pandamonium-backup` now has a shared `_is_skipped()` helper that always excludes `data/extension-runtimes` and `data/extensions/removed` from a snapshot, records both in the archive manifest's `exclusions`, and also skips their SQLite databases while staging the safe copies. The `--include-research` and `--include-attachments` behavior is unchanged. Extension runtimes are rehydrated on demand from the installed package revisions and the removed tree is never read back, so the rollback snapshot still carries the SQLite databases, keys, JSON state, uploads, personal docs, skills, and logical extension state.

### Product value and UI visibility

A normal update finishes in the same ballpark as the ~1.5-2 minute transactions observed before 2026-09-19, so the progress panel advances through "Protect local data" instead of appearing frozen at 55%. The updater panel, phases, and copy are unchanged; only the work behind them shrank. Rollback remains complete for everything the application actually owns.

### Verification

A new failure-first test `test_snapshot_skips_rederivable_extension_directories` failed on the original script and passes with the fix, asserting the two trees are absent from the archive members and listed in the manifest exclusions. `tests/test_backup_cli_security.py` plus `tests/test_release_updater.py` passed 46 checks. On CT103 an operator-approved cleanup removed the stale 1 GB `extensions/removed` graveyard and the orphaned 591 MB pandaflix runtime digest, taking the data directory from 3.2 GB to 1.6 GB; all six installed extensions remained and `/api/health` stayed healthy. Protected PR CI passed Python, browser, syntax, dependency, secret, workflow, container, and image gates.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, schema, environment variable, authentication, proxy contract, or stored-data change was introduced. The update backup intentionally no longer restores extension runtime toolchains or uninstall residue; those are rebuilt or re-derived after a rollback, while all user and logical extension data is still captured. This changes only the canonical `pandamonium-backup` snapshot scope used by the updater and the CLI.
